title: GJ 3323 extraction differences show excess 30-day grouping under a within-season shuffle model
abstract: We test time grouping in 121 same-exposure GJ 3323 HARPS velocity extraction differences. A within-season shuffle test of paired values and weights gives p = 0.0161 after a joint test of 3, 10 and 30 day bins. The strongest excess is at 30 days: the bin statistic is 0.21615, compared with a shuffle mean of 0.12242. Uniform weights give p = 0.0158. The early season alone does not resolve the effect. Removal of the two published waves gives a descriptive p = 0.0562. The result depends on within-season exchangeability and does not identify a cause. A common additive orbital shift cancels between the paired products. No new planet, stellar period or independent-instrument confirmation is found. Code, aggregate results, a figure, exact source provenance and separate-data reproduction steps are included. The external source table and record-level derivatives are excluded because redistribution rights were not established.

display.caption: Measured bin statistic and pointwise shuffle ranges at three scales. The combined three-scale p is 0.0161 for paired weights, 0.0158 for uniform weights, and 0.0562 after removing both published waves. These are conditional time tests, not planet probabilities.
